body:
Backing up @MrBrownieCGN's point 5 with measurements from the *other* side of the same coin. We run a
**userspace XDP datapath (eUPF)** in front of open5gs-smfd, and there the failure mode is the opposite
of what you describe for open5gs-upfd: instead of keeping sessions forever, the UPF tears down
**everything** on heartbeat loss — including the association.

Both behaviours sit on the same 3GPP ambiguity you quoted (TS 23.527 §4.4.3.1 "for a preconfigured
time ... shall delete all the session contexts"), so a **configurable** bound (per your point 5 and
@pespin's T_release_after_upf_failure in #4860) would be the right shape for both implementations.

**What we measured (eUPF, heartbeat_interval=5 s, retries=3)**

- SMF process frozen / unreachable for ~15 s → eUPF logs `the number of unanswered heartbeats` and
  **deletes the PFCP association and all sessions** (8 sessions → 0).
- With the sessions gone but traffic still arriving, every GTP-U packet hit `XDP_PASS` (no matching
  session) → kernel slow path → all 4 cores at 100%, i.e. the failure **amplifies** instead of
  degrading gracefully. Nothing self-recovered; we needed an SMF restart.
- Second occurrence (different trigger, same outcome): under 2.4 Mpps of GTP-U the userspace process
  was starved, missed its own heartbeats, and again dropped association + sessions — a **false
  positive** caused by local overload, not by an SMF failure at all.

That last point is the interesting one for this ticket: the "preconfigured time" needs a lower bound
that survives transient local overload, and it should be independent from the interval used to detect
peer failure. In our case 3 × 5 s = 15 s is far too eager: a 15 s CPU starvation window is exactly
what a traffic burst looks like on a 4-core edge box.

**Data points that may be useful for sizing the bound**

- Real UPF restart (our case: process restart, state lost): SMF detects via heartbeat give-up at
  **~11 s** and releases 8/8 sessions; UEs reactivate and everything is back **~4 s** after the UPF
  answers again (measured with default open5gs timers; this is the #4863 path).
- UPF side, if it keeps sessions (open5gs-upfd today): sessions survive, but traffic is black-holed
  until the SMF returns, and PFCP restoration only happens when the SMF comes back with a new
  Recovery Time Stamp.

So the two sides currently disagree about who blinks first, and the operator has no knob on either.
A single `T_release_after_upf_failure`-style timer with a sane default (and `-1` = keep forever) would
cover: open5gs-upfd keeping sessions (today), eUPF deleting them too early (today), and the
"keep sessions for a short outage" case everybody actually wants.

Happy to re-run our scenario (real NG interface, 8 PDU sessions, 4 UEs, VoLTE alongside) against
patches on either side and report timings — we already have the harness and the capture tooling from
the #4860 work.

Thanks for opening this, and thanks @zhangerfei-dp for the measurements from the other side. Agreed that the time
after which the UPF gives up on its sessions should be its own setting, separate from how fast a missing peer is
detected; with that split, a short detection window and a longer hold time no longer pull against each other. For the
detection side the separate heartbeat keys proposed in #4876 would apply; for the hold time see the last points below.

A few additions from reading main @ 310fea9 (code reading only, not run as a dedicated test):

- The only place the UPF deletes the sessions of a node is `pfcp_restoration()` (`src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:371-386`). It
  runs only when `restoration_required` is set, i.e. when the SMF is heard again with a newer Recovery Time Stamp
  (`lib/pfcp/handler.c:38-41`, `:75-78`). On a missing heartbeat the UPF just goes back to `will_associate`
  (`:342-346`). So an SMF that never comes back, or comes back without having restarted, leaves its sessions in the
  UPF.
- Network split: since #4863 the SMF releases its sessions when it loses the UPF, but its Session Deletion Requests
  cannot reach the UPF during the split. After the split heals the association is set up again without
  `restoration_required` (neither side restarted), so as far as we can see the UPF keeps sessions the SMF no longer
  has.
- open5gs-sgwud has the same path (`src/sgwu/pfcp-sm.c:316-319`, deletion only in `pfcp_restoration()` `:345-356`).
  TS 23.007 V18.5.0 has the corresponding rule for the EPC user plane, clause 16.1A.3:

  > When a SGW-U detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SGW-C is not reachable for a preconfigured time, the SGW-U
  > shall delete all session contexts affected by the unreachability of the peer PFCP entity in the SGW-C that it may
  > have stored.

  and clause 17.1A.3:

  > When a PGW-U detects that a peer PFCP entity in the PGW-C is not reachable for a preconfigured time, the PGW-U
  > shall delete all session contexts affected by the unreachability of the peer PFCP entity in the PGW-C that it may
  > have stored.

- One way to do it: start a per-node timer only when `will_associate` is entered because of the missing heartbeat
  (`:345`), not on the other transitions into that state (`:47`, `:231`, `:259`); stop it when the association is set
  up again; on expiry run the loop that `pfcp_restoration()` already has. Make the "preconfigured time" configurable,
  with `-1` for "never", counted from the heartbeat give-up rather than tied to the heartbeat interval. It should not
  be shorter than the SMF-side `T_release_after_upf_failure` discussed in #4860, so that an N4 interruption the SMF
  decides to ride out does not cost the UPF its sessions.
- If MPAS/SSET are implemented later, TS 23.527 clause 4.4.3.2 applies instead (only the feature bits exist today,
  `lib/pfcp/types.h:204`, `:246`).

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
Right now, lots of timer timeout values are calculated/derived based on the same time.message.duration value, which defaults to `local_conf.time.message.duration = ogs_time_from_sec(10)` and can be set through config file:
```
time:
  message:
    duration: 20000
```

This creates problems, since for instance in open5gs-smfd GTPv2C timeout values are set to the same values as PFCP ones, which is IMHO wrong, since in most cases (UE initiated procedures) the GTPv2C procedures will take more time than the PFCP procedures (ie. the later are inner steps of the former).

As a result, while the PFCP procedure is ongoing (or failing at some point), the GTPv2C gtp_xact may have been freed earlier, which means when the inner PGCP procedure finishes (correctly or not), there no way to reach back towards the UE.


In order to fix this, the ogs-config should have proper separation of config fields, one for each timeout, with a sane set of defaults (maybe also defaults tweaked by the application), which can then independently be modified through config file.
Extra logging warning the user can be added if some wrong configured is detected (like the PFCP timeout >= GTPv2C timeout mentioned above).

issue.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

TTCN-3 test SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout from osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git showcases the scenario:
https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Delete  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:836)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

TTCN-3

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

issue.body:
On heartbeat failure, the UPF only went back to will_associate and kept the sessions of that SMF. They were removed only when the SMF came back with a new Recovery Time Stamp.

Delete them on heartbeat failure (TS 23.527 4.4.3.1).

No separate hold timer is added. SGW-U still keeps its sessions, because SGW-C also keeps them on heartbeat failure; a comment is added there.

Issues: #4877

issue.title: [PFCP] Add release_after_peer_failure timer and PFCP Session Retention

repository.name: open5gs
repository.description: Open5GS is a C-language Open Source implementation for 5G Core and EPC, i.e. the core network of LTE/NR network (Release-19)

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
## Summary

When the PFCP heartbeat towards a peer gives up, the SMF releases all PDU sessions of that UPF at once (`reselect_upf()`, since #4863), and the UPF deletes all sessions of that SMF at once (92655020). As suggested by @pespin in #4860 (https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6575804663, design agreed in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6576234185), this adds a generic lib/pfcp timer, `pfcp.release_after_peer_failure` (seconds, default 0 = current behaviour): it is started when the heartbeat gives up and stopped when the node is associated again. While it runs, the sessions are kept; when it expires, the SMF releases them ("reactivation requested") and the UPF deletes them.

The second commit adds the PFCP Session Retention Information IE (TS 29.244 6.2.6.2), so that both sides agree on which sessions still exist when the association is set up again.

Rebased onto main, which now includes fc26daab9b (only operational sessions are restored after a UPF restart); the restoration in this PR goes through the same `pfcp_restoration()`. The first five commits are #4964 (timer duration 0, `ogs_assert(duration >= 0)` and the validation it needs); this PR will be rebased once #4964 is merged.

## Field motivation

- With the default timers the heartbeat gives up 7.5–18.5 s after the peer stops answering. A UPF that crashes and is restarted within a few seconds, or a short N4 path outage, therefore tears down every PDU session (for IMS: re-registration, dropped calls), although restoration (TS 23.527 4.3.2) or simply the still working data path would have kept them (#4860, comments 6202375701 and 6547687632).
- In an abts-based test with N4 blocked while GTP-U stays reachable (6547687632): both sides holding → 38/38 echo replies and no NGAP; UPF deleting at once while the SMF holds → 22 GTP-U Error Indications and no recovery after re-association. Hence one key for both NFs and a rule for their values.
- #4877: a userspace UPF that deletes on a short SMF stall amplifies the failure.

## Spec

- TS 23.527 4.3.3: "Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific."
- TS 23.527 4.4.3.1: "When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, ... the UPF shall delete all the session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored."
- TS 23.527 4.5: "If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart ... If the N4 path to the SMF is down, the UPF should handle this as a SMF Failure without Restart".
- TS 29.244 6.2.6.2.1/6.2.6.2.2, 7.4.4.1 (Table 7.4.4.1-2), 8.2.134 (PSREI), 8.2.135 (CP PFCP Entity IP Address).

## Fix

**`[PFCP] Add release_after_peer_failure timer`**
- lib/pfcp: `release_after_peer_failure` in `ogs_pfcp_context_t` (parsed under `<nf>.pfcp`; any value that fits `ogs_time_t`, invalid values fail the start), `t_release_after_peer_failure` in `ogs_pfcp_node_t`, `ogs_pfcp_node_start_release_after_peer_failure()`. Each NF creates/deletes the timer next to `t_no_heartbeat`. With 0 the timer is started with 0 and expires on the next poll, so the sessions are released right after the current events, as before.
- SMF/UPF: on heartbeat failure the node goes to will_associate as before (no new session selects it); with N > 0 the sessions are kept until the node is associated again or the timer expires. On the SMF, the sessions for which another associated UPF can be selected are released at once ("Reselect UPF"; moving a session to another UPF is not implemented). The timer also bounds the wait after a peer restart (newer Recovery Time Stamp).
- A timer event still queued after re-association, or after the timer was started again, is ignored.
- Sample configs document the key and the rule: the UPF value should not be shorter than the SMF value plus the heartbeat detection skew.

**`[PFCP] Retain kept sessions in Association Setup (TS 29.244 6.2.6.2)`**
- `node->num_of_sessions` counts the sessions bound to the node (`OGS_SETUP_PFCP_NODE()`/`OGS_CLEAR_PFCP_NODE()`). When the node fails with N > 0, the SMF takes `num_of_sessions_kept`. No session is bound to the node meanwhile, so a lower count means that a session was removed and its PFCP Session Deletion may not have reached the UPF; the IE selects the sessions per CP PFCP entity only, so then the SMF does not send it.
- The SMF includes the IE (with its CP PFCP Entity IP Address) while all kept sessions are still there and not yet released on expiry; the UPF retains the sessions of the node and sets PSREI if the IE is present, otherwise deletes them (6.2.6.2.2), also when they are kept in will_associate.
- Only the answer to the last Association Setup Request decides: PSREI set but sessions removed or released since the request was built → a new request without the IE; no PSREI → the kept sessions are restored regardless of the Recovery Time Stamp; sessions released on expiry are neither retained nor restored.
- An association set up by the UPF carries no retention information: the SMF follows with its own request. A node with a pending decision is not selectable, also not through the fallback of the UPF selection.

## Out of scope

- SGW-C/SGW-U: both keep their sessions on heartbeat failure today (comment in 92655020). They follow in a separate PR together (TS 23.007 16.1A.3/16.1A.4); until then they log that the key is ignored.
- AMF handling of PDU Session Resource Notify (TS 23.527 5.3.3.1): separate change, as announced in #4860.
- Retention per CP PFCP entity in the UPF (Open5GS CP functions have a single PFCP entity). If a session was removed during the outage, the kept ones are restored instead of retained, which interrupts their data path briefly.
- PFCP session requests sent to a kept node before it is associated again time out, as during heartbeat detection today.

## Configuration example

```yaml
smf:
  pfcp:
    release_after_peer_failure: 30
upf:
  pfcp:
    release_after_peer_failure: 60
```

## Refs

- Refs #4860 (comments 6575804663 and 6576234185), #4877
- Refs #4876 (separate heartbeat keys would make the detection skew configurable)

## Test plan

- [x] Each of the seven commits builds with `-Dwerror=true` on `main @ d9c44d67f`, and the `core` and `unit` test programs pass on each.
- [x] On the last commit: `tests/pfcp-peer-failure` (6 cases) and the suites registration, vonr, slice, handover, transfer, non3gpp, eir, attach, volte, csfb, 310014 pass.
- [x] `tests/pfcp-peer-failure` (SMF 40 s, UPF 30 s; a peer is made unreachable without a restart with SIGSTOP/SIGCONT; PFCP Session Establishment Requests counted on the metrics server of the UPF): UPF down 25 s then back → PDU session kept and retained, not restored; UPF stays down → released on expiry, no session left in the UPF after the next association; second UPF → released at once, new session on the other UPF; one of two sessions released during the outage → the UPF deletes both, the SMF restores the kept one; released on expiry and the release not answered yet when the UPF comes back → neither retained nor restored (new); SMF stays down → data path keeps working, deleted on expiry.
- [x] With `node->sessions_kept` removed (suggested in review), the second and the new case fail: the UPF keeps the released session after the SMF has removed it.
- [x] `tests/unit/pfcp-retention-test.c`: counting, all kept sessions there (IE), one removed during the failure, also across a second failure (no IE), released on expiry then failed again (no IE), no sessions.
- [ ] Not yet run against a real RAN; @zhangerfei-dp offered to run the stop/start UPF scenario in #4860.
